A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COD research. All 21 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Reorganized material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training and evaluation results, including 70B performance predictions in Table 3, pilot experiments and main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds predicted versus actual 70B performance after high-quality continued pretraining in Appendix D, Table A3.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 relaxes the reported cluster-filtering condition from 0 < c < 1 to 0 ≤ c < 1. Otherwise, the four-stage COD pipeline, improved MeanShift pseudocode, fitting formula and quartic mapping remain unchanged. The continued-pretraining experiment reuses the pipeline and existing cluster labels.

E1.justification: The eight downstream benchmarks and pilot-study tasks are retained. Appendix D adds evaluation under a high-quality continued-pretraining data regime, extending training-distribution coverage beyond v1's constant-distribution setting without adding downstream task domains or benchmark datasets.

E2.justification: The end-to-end, passrate-compute and loss-intermediate baselines remain, alongside the same COD variants, clustering algorithms, fitting formulas, anchors and interpolation comparators. The new continued-pretraining table reports COD alone; its motivating citations do not constitute additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds a separate continued-pretraining protocol across the model suite: high-quality data and learning-rate decay, matched phase distributions and token-to-parameter ratios, 3B–1,000B additional training tokens, and final-checkpoint evaluation using prior cluster labels. This substantially extends the evaluation design. Existing benchmark sample counts, few-shot settings and original training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D newly tests whether previously obtained clusters and COD predictions remain useful after continued pretraining with changed data and learning-rate conditions. This adds a limited robustness question. The earlier clustering, formula, anchor and interpolation ablations, and difficulty-distribution analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: The 100 evaluation trials and averaging across three adjacent checkpoints remain documented in Appendix A.2. Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new continued-pretraining table adds point estimates without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Table A3 adds predicted and actual continued-pretraining results across all eight benchmarks, with mean error 2.33 percentage points and errors ranging from 0.20 to 4.93. These concern different training conditions, not improved same-setting performance. Earlier result tables are numerically retained, including COD's 1.63 mean and 2.38 maximum error. V2 additionally states 1.68% in Section 5.2, contradicting its unchanged table.

T1.justification: Appendix B's scaling-law statement, Eq. (9), changes its correction term from σ²/(2μ) to σ²/μ; the main proof sketch changes similarly. However, the lemma and concluding derivation retain σ²/(2μ), leaving a statement–proof inconsistency. Most mathematics is unchanged; renaming propositions as theorems adds no theoretical substance.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: difficulty-based clustering, a theoretically motivated performance scaling law, predictable-subset extrapolation and mapping to full-set performance. The 70B, eight-benchmark headline claim of 1.36% is also retained. Condensed wording does not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V1 explicitly identifies annealing as untested; v2 removes that exclusion and discusses continued-pretraining applicability in Appendix D. It adds hypotheses linking larger MATH, GSM8k and TriviaQA errors to training-data correlation, bias and metric volatility. The limitations concerning MoE models, insufficient evaluation samples and chain-of-thought theory remain in Appendix G.

D1.justification: V2 newly discloses a short warmup, an example radius for Improved-KMeans, and continued-pretraining token budgets and checkpoint selection. Conversely, Table A1 omits v1 Table 2's layer-count row, and the description of COD without mapping drops its explicit K-Means specification. These documentation changes do not establish altered architectures or rerun original experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds DeepSeek-v3 to motivate continued pretraining, removes the Elbow-method and Silhouette references, and explicitly characterizes the GPT-4 report's subset prediction as failing to predict the full set. Additional Llama 3 and Qwen2.5 bibliography entries duplicate works already cited rather than introducing distinct prior research.

P1.justification: The abstract, method explanations and experimental discussion undergo extensive condensation and rewriting. Separate ablation sections become subsections of Section 5.3, experimental settings move to Appendix C, and limitations are consolidated in Appendix G. The unused vertical-smoothing discussion is removed. This substantially reorganizes the narrative despite retaining most scientific content.

P2.justification: V2 introduces a substantially different document design with branding, blue headings, changed typography and wider text blocks. Figure 2 is redrawn, Figure 1's cluster legends become subset legends, captions are revised, the dataset table is transposed, and configuration tables move to the appendix. A continued-pretraining results table is added; the earlier result plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix D provides useful evidence for high-quality continued pretraining, an explicitly untested limitation in v1, with budgets, predicted and actual outcomes, and discussion of larger errors. This modestly improves practical coverage. The gain is constrained by absent comparative baselines and uncertainty estimates for that regime, omitted layer counts, the new 1.68% prose/table discrepancy, and the appendix theorem coefficient now conflicting with its derivation. The original comparative evidence is unchanged.
